title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out at the display layer of a financial service. The trading app the couple used was legitimate, but the screen showing Jerry Dunaway his balances and returns was not, a fabricated site that the reporting says was built using artificial intelligence. The failure is not a model stating something false in passing. It is a counterfeit interface presented as an account record, and from the screen alone the two were indistinguishable to the person reading it.

The deception worked because it sat on top of a real product. Small withdrawals were allowed at first, which made the account appear to function, and the false balances then supported larger transfers. Catching it would have required confirming the account through something the other party did not control, such as the legitimate app or the platform behind it, rather than through the interface the scammer supplied. Nothing in the reporting indicates any check of that kind happened before the money was gone.

What is not established is who ran the scam, which AI tool or method produced the fake site, and whether any of the money will be recovered. Gwinnett County police are investigating, and an investigation is not a finding. The observation that victims in similar cases rarely recover their funds describes a pattern, not the outcome here.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started when a stranger contacted them through WhatsApp. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, initially allowing small withdrawals to build trust before gradually increasing the investment amounts. The couple later discovered that while the app was legitimate, scammers had created a fake digital site using artificial intelligence that showed false account balances and investment returns on Jerry's screen.

The Dunaways are now speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers. Jerry and Mindy describe feeling angry, embarrassed, and financially devastated after losing their life savings. Gwinnett County police are investigating the case, though authorities note that victims in similar situations rarely recover their stolen funds. The couple's children have created a GoFundMe campaign to help their parents cover daily expenses as they work to rebuild their lives.
